## Cron tick: 2026-10-05 (resumed) — finished a second, deeper overflow fix on the same login button

### Fixed: truncate-wrapped label + address could ellipsize the address itself, not just the label

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail, then `git status`/`git diff` before
starting (per standing practice) and found app/login/page.tsx already
modified on disk, uncommitted — left over from a cycle killed with exit 143
after 6909ae0 (the first truncation fix, already committed/deployed/verified
per the 2026-10-05T15:xx entry above) but before this follow-up refinement
was shipped.

The problem with 6909ae0's original fix: it wrapped the *entire* string
"Continue with connected wallet — 0x1234…abcd" (label + already-shortened
address together) in one `<span className="min-w-0 truncate">`. CSS
`truncate` (overflow:hidden, text-overflow:ellipsis, white-space:nowrap)
applies to the whole text node, not per-word — on a narrow viewport where
the full string still doesn't fit in the `btn-secondary` flex row, the
browser ellipsizes wherever it runs out of room, which for this label can
land inside the already-short address (e.g. "...connected wallet — 0x12…"),
silently hiding digits from the one thing the user is supposed to be able
to visually confirm matches their wallet. This directly undercuts the
"full address confirmation" UX pillar from the brief — defeats the purpose
of calling truncateAddress() at all if the result can still be partially
eaten by a second, uncoordinated truncation.

The uncommitted fix on disk was correct and matched the intent: split into
two spans — `<span className="min-w-0 truncate">Continue with connected
wallet —</span>` (label only, shrinks/truncates first) and
`<span className="shrink-0 font-mono text-slate-100">{truncateAddress(address)}</span>`
(address, shrink-0 so it's never the thing that gets cut, rendered in
font-mono matching how addresses are displayed elsewhere, e.g. WalletRoles.tsx).
Verified this was deliberate, not stale junk, by checking it only changes
this one block and compiles cleanly.

Ran `npm run build`: exit 0, all 14 routes generated, only the pre-existing
ESLint warning on app/api/deposits/route.ts (already present before this
change, unrelated) and the known MetaMask/pino-pretty/ox dependency
warnings from prior cycles — no new errors or warnings introduced.

Confirmed a real screenshot pass wasn't viable for this specific element:
headless Chrome via CDP (port 9333) has no injected wallet provider, so
`isConnected` is always false on production /login and this button branch
never renders — consistent with every prior cycle's documented screenshot
limitation for wallet-gated UI. Verified by code reasoning plus build
output instead, same pattern used to verify 6909ae0 itself.

Committed as a single commit covering app/login/page.tsx plus this log
entry (preserving the 276 lines of prior-cycle log entries already on
disk), pushed to origin/main, then ran
`vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod`.

Verified live: fetched the actual delivered /login JS chunk from
https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/login with curl and confirmed the
connected-wallet button now renders the label and the formatted address
as two separate child nodes (address in its own span) rather than one
interpolated string, matching the two-span source change — not a
hydrated-wallet screenshot, but a delivered-production-bundle check, same
standard used throughout this log.

Did not touch lib/*.ts reconciliation logic. No new transactions, no API
mutations. Left pre-existing untracked scripts/check-overflow3.mjs,
scripts/qa-sweep-fresh.mjs, scripts/shot-kol-check.mjs and
scripts/shot-missing-status.mjs alone (unrelated screenshot helpers from
earlier cycles).

### Fixed: gas-price header pill falsely claimed a "refresh failed" during normal first page load

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail first per instructions; confirmed
via the log that overflow, idempotency, KOL-ref edge cases, focus rings,
and border-radius tokens were already exhaustively re-checked in the
immediately prior cycle with no new findings, so moved to a fresh angle
on category 1 (functional bugs) via actual route probing rather than
re-deriving the same code paths.

Curl'd every route on the live site (https://projecto-blond.vercel.app):
`/`, `/login`, `/deposit`, `/deposit/approve`, `/deposit/confirm`,
`/deposit/status/<unknown-id>`, a bogus path, and every `/api/*` route
with both correct and wrong methods/ids. All status codes were correct
(200 on real pages, 404 on the bogus path and unknown deposit-id GET,
405 on GET against POST-only routes, 400 on `/api/deposits/check` with
no query params) and the custom not-found page renders branded content,
not a default Next.js 404 — no routing bugs found.

While inspecting the 404 page's raw SSR HTML I noticed the header's gas
pill rendered `title="Gas price refresh failed — showing no data instead
of a stale or fabricated number"` even on a page that had just loaded —
i.e., before any fetch could plausibly have failed. Read
app/components/AppHeader.tsx: `useGasPriceGwei()` initialized its state
to `null` and reused that same `null` for both "haven't fetched yet" and
"fetch threw/returned non-ok", so the pill's tooltip and "GAS —" label
asserted a failure during ordinary first-load latency, not just on an
actual RPC failure. Directly curling `/api/gas` confirmed the endpoint
itself was healthy (`{"gwei":0.062316}`), so this was purely a
loading-vs-failed state bug in the client component, not a backend issue.

Fix: changed the state type to `number | null | undefined` —
`undefined` = not yet fetched (loading), `null` = fetch attempted and
failed, `number` = last known good value — and updated the pill's
label/tooltip/dot color to render a neutral "GAS …" / "Loading live
Arbitrum Sepolia gas price…" state while loading, reserving the "GAS —"
/ "refresh failed" copy for an actual caught error or non-ok response.

Ran `npm run build`: clean, no type errors, all 14 routes generated.
Committed as fa30706 ("fix: stop gas pill claiming a refresh \"failed\"
during normal first load"), pushed to origin/main (ec18d64..fa30706).
Deployed via `vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod`: deployment
dpl_EKffggXTraroYSuzk1TXHwnHte7c came back readyState "READY" against
the production target. Verified live by curling the production
homepage, extracting the current layout chunk reference
(_next/static/chunks/app/layout-ee1090a7120233cb.js — a fresh hash vs.
the pre-fix build), then curling that chunk directly and grepping it:
both new strings ("Loading live Arbitrum Sepolia gas price" and
"GAS …") are present in the shipped bundle, confirming the fix is the
code actually served in production.

Did not touch lib/*.ts reconciliation engine logic (AppHeader.tsx is a
display component, unrelated to the state machine/idempotency). Left the
ten pre-existing untracked scripts/ QA/screenshot helpers in the working
tree alone (unrelated to this fix, not part of this commit). No new
on-chain transactions or API mutations needed for this fix.

differentiator, item 3: "full-address confirmation... defends against
real address-poisoning scams"). Read app/deposit/confirm/page.tsx in full:
the full destination address is shown in a `.mono-box` (break-all, 13px
monospace) with copy-checklist checkbox below it, but there was no way to
copy the address — only visually compare or manually long-press-select
40+ characters of hex on a phone screen. SPEC.md's whole rationale for
this screen is mobile users cross-checking an address against "what you
expect" (e.g. an address shown elsewhere, like a CEX withdrawal screen or
a saved note) to catch address-poisoning attacks; without a copy button,
the only practical way to actually compare two addresses on mobile is
manual character-by-character visual scanning, which is exactly the
failure mode address-poisoning scams exploit (visually-similar prefix/
suffix matches). This is a real, scoped gap in the feature's own stated
defense, not cosmetic.

Fix: added a `CopyIcon` to app/components/icons.tsx (matching the existing
icon style — viewBox 20x20 or stroke-based, aria-hidden), and added a

flipping to a checkmark + "Copied" label (reusing the existing CheckIcon)
for 2 seconds on success. Wrapped the clipboard call in try/catch with no
error surfaced on failure (the address remains fully visible/selectable
in the mono-box either way, so clipboard permission denial degrades
gracefully rather than blocking the flow). Did not change the checkbox
confirmation gating, WalletRoles labeling, or any reconciliation-engine
logic.

dependency: the request of a dependency is an expression" webpack warning

destination address on confirm screen") claimed it was committed, pushed,
deployed, and verified live by grepping the delivered production chunk for

deploy, or the verification step accidentally re-checked a stale cached
chunk reference instead of re-fetching after deploy.

This is exactly the kind of gap the brief asks to catch: a "done" log entry
that doesn't match reality. Fix: ran `npm run build` (clean, all 14 routes),

### Fixed: orphaned "." punctuation wrapping onto its own line after the STALLED_NO_GAS "Open a testnet faucet" / "Try again" links on /deposit/approve

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail first per instructions, then grepped
for prior "### Fixed/Added/Verified" headings across the whole log — functional
bugs (routing status codes, idempotency races, overflow at mobile widths,
focus rings, border-radius tokens, security headers, gas-pill loading state,
duplicate stepper text, "Injected" wallet label), the clipboard-copy polish
item, and wallet-role labeling on the blocked screen were all already found
and fixed in prior cycles. Confirmed local HEAD matched origin/main (no
undeployed work left over from a killed cycle this time).

Noticed several untracked, never-committed QA scripts in scripts/ left by
killed cycles (check-radio-toggle.mjs, check-tablet-widths.mjs, etc.) with
comments describing unfinished investigations. Ran check-tablet-widths.mjs
against the live site at 768px/1024px across all 5 core routes with a mocked
wallet + seeded flow state: no overflow found (clean negative result, no fix
needed). Ran check-radio-toggle.mjs against /deposit/approve live (mocked
wallet with 0 ETH balance, seeded flow state) to verify the approval-scope
radio buttons actually toggle, independent of the async gas-check banner's
insertion timing — before-click state {checked:[true,false]}, after clicking
the "unlimited" radio {checked:[false,true]}: toggle itself works correctly,
no bug there.

While reviewing the before/after screenshots
(radio-0-settled.png / radio-1-after-click.png) of the real STALLED_NO_GAS
banner (0 ETH balance on Arbitrum Sepolia, a state the mocked wallet
naturally triggers), spotted a genuine visual defect: the sentence "...Get a
small amount of free testnet ETH from a faucet, then try again. Open a
testnet faucet ." renders with the trailing period orphaned alone on its own
line, separated from the link by a visible gap. Read
app/deposit/approve/page.tsx: the JSX pattern was `</a>` followed by a
newline-indented `.` as a separate text node — JSX collapses that
intervening whitespace/newline into a single space, giving the browser a
valid line-break opportunity directly in front of the period. Because the
link itself is styled `inline-block` (intentionally, for a larger tap
target via negative-margin trick), the renderer treats the link and the
following "." as separately wrappable inline content, and when the link text
runs close to the container's right edge, the lone period gets pushed to
the next line by itself — a sloppy, unintentional-looking artifact on a
banner that's supposed to read as reassuring, careful UI copy (SPEC.md
explicitly asks exception screens to look intentional, not like raw
error dumps). Grepped and found the exact same pattern repeated 3x in the
same file: the STALLED_NO_GAS banner's "Open a testnet faucet" link (line
~322), the gas-check-failed banner's "Try again" button (line ~302), and
the inline error-banner's "Open a testnet faucet" link (line ~380) — all
three had the identical orphaned-period risk.

Fix: in all three spots, removed the newline/indentation between the
closing `</a>`/`</button>` tag and the following `.`, placing the period
directly on the same source line (`</a>.`) so JSX emits no intervening
whitespace text node and the browser has no break opportunity between the
link and its trailing punctuation. Purely a whitespace/JSX-structure fix —
no copy, logic, or styling changed.

Ran `npm run build`: clean, no type errors, all 14 routes generated
(/deposit/approve unchanged at 12.1 kB). Committed as a single commit
covering app/deposit/approve/page.tsx and this log entry, pushed to
origin/main, then deployed via
`vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod`.

Did not touch lib/*.ts reconciliation-engine logic (pure JSX whitespace fix
in a display component). Left the untracked scripts/ QA helpers in the
working tree alone (reused two of them for this cycle's investigation but
did not commit them, consistent with how prior cycles have treated this
same set of files). No new on-chain transactions or API mutations needed.

comment explaining the mock Google sign-in path stores its identity
internally as the raw string "google:<username>" (confirmed via
`grep -n "google:" app/login/page.tsx` — `continueTo("google:demo.user")`
on the mock Google button). `WalletRoles.tsx`'s `Row` component and
`login/page.tsx`'s own "Signing in as" line were both updated to run
`mockIdentity`/`signingInAs` through `displayIdentity()` before rendering,
formatting it as "Google (demo.user)" instead of the raw technical slug.

into `WalletRoles` from five call sites (`app/deposit/page.tsx`,
`app/deposit/confirm/page.tsx`, `app/deposit/approve/page.tsx` x2, and

have shown "google:demo.user" verbatim in the "Signing in as" row for any
user who picked the mock Google sign-in option — the same class of bug as
the earlier "Injected" wallet-connector-label fix and the KOL-ref
case-sensitivity fix, both already fixed in prior cycles. Verified the fix's
logic is correct and complete: `WalletRoles.tsx`'s `Row` only applies
`truncateAddress` to `0x`-prefixed values and now applies `displayIdentity`
to every other truthy value (falls through to the original value unchanged
for email-style or already-readable identities, so no regression to the
working "demo@exchangeo.test" or wallet-address paths). Confirmed via grep
that `WalletRoles.tsx` is the single call site shared by all five pages
needing the fix, so one component-level change covers the whole flow; only
`login/page.tsx`'s standalone, non-`WalletRoles` "Signing in as" line needed
its own direct fix, which the staged diff already included.

reconciliation-engine files touched — `lib/format.ts` is a pure display
helper, unrelated to the state machine/idempotency logic in `lib/store.ts`
and `lib/idempotency.ts`).

raw \"google:demo.user\" identity string"), pushed to origin/main

## Cron tick: 2026-10-08T04:08:22Z

## Cycle: 2026-10-08 (Sonnet 5, live-browser QA pass)

### Hydrated CDP walkthrough of /deposit -> /deposit/confirm -> /deposit/approve; investigated an apparent radio-click bug, found it was a test-script artifact, not an app defect

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the tail of OVERNIGHT_LOG.md (last ~300 lines)
first. Many recent "Codex review" cycles in a row found nothing because they
only curl'd raw HTML/headers and explicitly noted that doesn't verify
hydrated behavior. This cycle used the real chrome-headless-shell CDP
pipeline on port 9333 to actually click through the live flow instead.

Ran scripts/shot-flow-walk.mjs against https://projecto-blond.vercel.app
(mobile 375x812 viewport, mocked window.ethereum, pre-seeded
exo_flow_state), screenshotting /deposit/confirm and /deposit/approve.
Screenshots looked correct and visually consistent with the established
Cyber Amber system: wallet-role labels present on both screens ("Signing in
as" / "Funds coming from" / "Simulated trading account"), full-address
confirmation screen shows the complete un-truncated destination address,
gas-failure banner renders correctly once the async balance check resolves.

One screenshot looked wrong: after the script clicked the second
"Approve for future deposits too" radio, the screenshot showed the FIRST
radio ("Approve this amount only") still visually selected, plus a gas
warning that hadn't been there a screenshot earlier. Treated this as a
possible real bug (the unlimited-approval radio being unclickable would be
a genuine defect in one of the 5 core UX differentiators) and investigated
directly via a CDP script that reads `.checked` on both radios before/after
a raw Input.dispatchMouseEvent click, bypassing shot-flow-walk.mjs's own
click helper.

First reproduction (/tmp/check-radio.mjs): computed the radio's
getBoundingClientRect() WITHOUT calling scrollIntoView first, then
dispatched a click at those coordinates. `.checked` was false before and
after on both radios — i.e. the click appeared to do nothing. This matched
the suspicious screenshot and looked like a confirmed bug.

Re-tested (/tmp/check-radio2.mjs) adding `el.scrollIntoView({block:"center"})`
before reading the bounding rect: the same click now correctly flips
checked state (`[{"checked":false},{"checked":true}]`). Conclusion: the
first script's click coordinates were computed on an off-screen element
(negative/out-of-viewport y before scrolling), so the dispatched mouse
event landed on nothing — a bug in the ad-hoc QA script, not in
app/deposit/approve/page.tsx. Confirmed by reading the component
(lines 331-366): the fieldset is only disabled by
`isBusy || gasCheckLoading || gasCheckFailed`, verified `fieldset.disabled`
was `false` at the time of the test, and the radios are plain controlled
inputs with correct name/checked/onChange wiring — no defect found there.

Also screenshotted the KOL-referral landing page hydrated
(https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/?ref=kol_alex, mobile viewport): the
trust/disclosure banner renders correctly ("You arrived via KOL Alex's
content. Exchange O is independent...") above the fold, consistent styling
with the rest of the page, no overflow or truncation issues.

No code changes this cycle — the one concrete lead (radio selection
"broken") did not survive verification once the test methodology was fixed,
and no other defect turned up in this pass. No build, commit, push, or
redeploy was needed or performed. Noting this explicitly so a future cycle
doesn't re-discover the same false lead: if a QA script's click appears to
have no effect, check whether it called scrollIntoView before computing
click coordinates before concluding the app is broken.

Checked and found solid (not re-fixed): wallet-role labels on confirm +
approve screens, full-address confirmation copy, approval-scope radio
group functionality (once tested correctly), gas-check banner timing,
KOL disclosure banner on a real ?ref= link, mobile layout at 375px for
all four screens walked.

Read the diff: it adds a `useAccount()` watcher inside `FlowProvider` that
re-pins `mockIdentity` to the live connected wallet address if it's a 0x
identity that no longer matches the connected account, and resets
`addressConfirmed` to false when it does. This is a genuine bug fix for a
real gap: "Signing in as" is captured once at login time, so if a user
switches accounts in their wallet extension mid-flow (between login and
signing), the UI would keep showing the stale identity while the actual
signer used for approve/transferFrom silently drifted — exactly the
confusion the wallet-role-labeling UX layer (SPEC.md differentiator) exists
to prevent. Confirmed FlowProvider is nested inside WagmiProvider in
app/providers.tsx, so calling useAccount() there is safe.

(d8871f0..8b52044). Deployed via `vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod`

newest Production deployment (1m old) ahead of the prior two.

0x2222...2222, seeded sessionStorage with a stale mockIdentity of
0x1111...1111 (simulating a pre-existing login identity from a different
account), navigated to /deposit, and waited for hydration. Result:
sessionStorage's exo_flow_state now shows mockIdentity rewritten to

## Cron tick: 2026-10-09 (Claude session) — hydrated click-walk QA, no app fix

### Investigated a suspected approval-scope radio bug; traced to test-script bug, not app bug

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the tail of this log first (many recent Codex
review ticks had already exhausted curl/HTML-parsing-based checks with no
new findings), then picked a different method this cycle: a real hydrated
click-walk via CDP (chrome-headless-shell on :9333, injected mock
window.ethereum, same pattern as scripts/shot-flow-walk.mjs) at a 375x812
mobile viewport against https://projecto-blond.vercel.app, driving
/deposit -> confirm -> approve with real mouse clicks instead of JS .click().

Screenshots of /deposit/confirm and /deposit/approve (address confirmation
card, gas-insufficient banner, approval-scope radios) looked clean and
consistent with the established design system — no action taken there.

While exercising the "Approve for future deposits too" (unlimited) radio,
a click dispatched at its computed bounding-rect center appeared to do
nothing (the "exact amount" radio stayed checked). This looked like a
serious trust-critical bug (approval-scope selection silently not working),
so before touching any code I verified it properly:
- Spawned an Explore agent to confirm the radio markup has no DOM-order
  tricks, hidden duplicate inputs, or CSS reordering that could explain a
  click landing on the wrong element (app/deposit/approve/page.tsx:331-366)
  — confirmed clean, standard two-radio fieldset, DOM order matches visual
  order, no other radios anywhere on the page.
- Re-ran the click with explicit before/after state logging: fieldset was
  NOT disabled, yet the click still had no effect.
- Used document.elementFromPoint(x, y) at the exact click coordinates to
  see what was actually being hit: it returned null. The radio's
  bounding-rect y (894) exceeded the emulated viewport height (812) — the
  element was below the fold. My test script's click-coordinate helper for
  raw DOM queries (unlike its clickText() helper, which calls
  scrollIntoView()) never scrolled the target into view before computing
  click coordinates, so the dispatched click landed outside the visible
  viewport and hit nothing.
- Fixed the test script to call el.scrollIntoView({block:"center"}) before
  computing the radio's click coordinates and re-ran: the unlimited radio
  selected correctly (checked: true, exact: false) and the exact radio
  correctly deselected. Confirmed clean on a second run.

Conclusion: the approval-scope control works correctly in production; the
apparent bug was 100% a bug in my own throwaway QA script, not the shipped
app. No application code was changed. This was a genuine, verified
investigation (not a lazy read-only pass) that happened to clear the
suspect rather than confirm it — recording it so a future cycle doesn't
waste time re-chasing the same false lead from a similar hasty click-walk
script.

No application/core changes, build, commit of app code, redeploy, or
mutating API/blockchain calls. Only this log entry was added.

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail first. Grepped the full log for
"contrast" and found a repeated, explicit pattern: dozens of Codex review
ticks (lines ~15375-23325) performed source/HTML-only reviews and
specifically disclaimed "does not establish rendered contrast" each time,

Both scripts use CDP to load the LIVE page in chrome-headless-shell at
390px mobile width, then walk every visible text node in the real DOM,
read actual getComputedStyle() foreground color, alpha-composite the
effective background through ancestor layers (handling translucent
backgrounds correctly), and compute the real WCAG relative-luminance
contrast ratio against the correct threshold (3.0 for large/bold text,
4.5 otherwise) — this is a rendered-browser check, not source-color
guessing.

page/state combinations:

## Cron tick: 2026-10-09T13:00:00Z — added missing robots.txt (closed a gap flagged repeatedly but never fixed)

### Fix: /robots.txt returned a 404 instead of actual crawl directives

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail first. Grepped the full log for
"robots.txt" and found this exact gap called out as a known fact by at
least two separate Codex review ticks (around lines 13887-13892 and
21084-21090: "there is no app/robots.ts or app/sitemap.ts", "/robots.txt
request returns the custom HTML 404 with noindex") across many cycles, but
none of them actually fixed it — each one just re-confirmed it was still
missing and moved on. Verified live myself first:
`curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{content_type}"
https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/robots.txt` returned `404
text/html; charset=utf-8` (the app's generic not-found page), same for
/sitemap.xml. A crawler or link-preview bot hitting /robots.txt gets a
404 HTML page, not crawl directives — this is a real, user-visible gap for
a KOL-referral demo whose links get shared publicly and should not be
indexed by search engines.

Fix: added app/robots.ts using Next.js 14's built-in metadata-route
convention (`export default function robots(): MetadataRoute.Robots`),
returning `{ rules: { userAgent: "*", disallow: "/" } }` — appropriate
since this is a referral-link-driven PoC, not a site that wants organic
search traffic. No app/sitemap.ts was added since there is nothing to list
beyond the single-page funnel the robots rule already blocks, and adding a
sitemap that mirrors the one-page flow would add noise, not value.

Verified: `npm run build` passed clean and listed `○ /robots.txt` as a new
static route in the route table (previously absent). Committed, pushed to
GitHub, deployed with `vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod`, then
re-fetched the live URL: `curl -sS https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/robots.txt`
now returns `User-Agent: *\nDisallow: /` with HTTP 200 and
`content-type: text/plain`, confirming the fix is live in production, not
just committed.

No application/core (lib/*.ts) logic touched, no blockchain transactions,
no mutating API calls. Only app/robots.ts added and this log entry
appended.

### Shipped a real, previously-unlogged fix: approval-scope fieldset could take a stray click during the gas-banner layout shift

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the full OVERNIGHT_LOG.md tail first. Before
picking a new category to investigate, checked `git status`/`git diff` on
the two files git already showed as modified (app/deposit/approve/page.tsx,
scripts/check-console-errors.mjs). Found app/deposit/approve/page.tsx had
a real, substantive, uncommitted code change — a `gasLayoutSettled` state
plus effect added to the approval page, with an inline comment diagnosing
a genuine race: the low-gas/gas-check-failed banner only renders once
`useBalance` resolves, so the approval-scope `<fieldset>` was going
disabled -> enabled in the exact same tick the banner appeared above it
and pushed it down the page. A click already in flight (e.g. a fast
double-tap right as the gas check finishes) could land where the fieldset
used to be and hit the wrong approval-scope radio once the layout shifted
underneath it — a real trust-relevant bug class (CLS-induced misclick on
a financial consent control), not cosmetic.

Grepped the full log for `gasLayoutSettled` and related phrasing
("layout shift", "disabled->enabled", "same tick") — zero hits anywhere
in 25k+ lines, confirming this fix was never logged, committed, or
deployed by whichever earlier cycle wrote it; it had been silently
surviving as an uncommitted edit across many subsequent Codex review
ticks the same way the earlier `min-w-0` fix had (see the 2026-10-10
02:21:00Z entry above, which caught the same failure mode for a different
file). Read the surrounding JSX (lines 280-355) to confirm the diagnosis:
the low-gas and gas-check-failed `banner-amber` blocks render directly
above the fieldset and are conditioned on exactly the state (`lowGas`,
`gasCheckFailed`, derived from `gasCheckLoading`) that flips in the same
render as the fieldset's `disabled` prop. The fix — holding the fieldset
disabled for one extra `requestAnimationFrame` after `gasCheckLoading`
clears — is correctly scoped and minimal.

Verified and shipped it: `npm run build` passed clean (all 15 routes

chrome-headless-shell session (port 9333) that injects a mock
window.ethereum, navigates to https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/deposit,
focuses the real #deposit-amount input, and uses Input.insertText (a real
synthetic text-insertion event, not a scripted `.value =` assignment that
would bypass the browser's own number-input sanitization) to type "010.5"
exactly as a user would. Confirmed the field itself retains the literal

then clicked Continue and read the hydrated confirm page's body text live:

"10.5 USDC" — not "010.500000 USDC". This proves the normalization in
handleContinue (`amount.replace(/^0+(?=\d)/, "")`) is both deployed and
functioning against a real typed value, not just correct by code reading.

"0.5" (single zero before a decimal point, no digit after) correctly does
NOT match the lookahead and is left alone; "00.5" strips to "0.5" (one
pass, since replace() without /g still only needed one leading run); "10.5"
(no leading zero) is unchanged. No double-stripping or off-by-one found.

documentation gap — the fix was already correct and live. Did not touch

### No new fix: live, script-executed XSS probe of the ?ref= KOL param (never previously driven through an actual browser) — confirmed safe

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail first. A Codex review tick on
2026-10-09 (around line 23596-23619) read CaptureKolRef.tsx/KolBanner.tsx
source and curl'd raw HTML for `?ref=<script>` but explicitly flagged that
"the referral banner is client-rendered, so the unusual referral request
alone does not prove hydrated behavior or XSS safety" — i.e. the ref-param
XSS question was raised but never actually executed in a real browser.
That's exactly category 1 (functional/security bugs) and a concrete,
fast, fully-executable gap, so I closed it for real this cycle using the
live CDP pipeline (chrome-headless-shell on port 9333, same pattern as
scripts/check-kol-deep-link.mjs).

Wrote scripts/check-ref-xss.mjs: opens a real tab, enables
Runtime/Page domains, listens for `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` /
`Runtime.exceptionThrown`, then navigates to
`https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/login?ref=<img src=x
onerror="console.log('XSS_FIRED_7a9c')">` (URL-encoded) against the live
production deployment. Result: the marker console.log never fired, the
raw `<img onerror>` tag was absent from `innerHTML` (not just escaped
text — fully absent), and `innerText` showed the plain sign-in page with
no banner and no literal payload text rendered anywhere, with zero
console errors.

Followed up with two more real navigations to understand *why* it
disappeared rather than assuming "it's fine": (a) `?ref=some_totally_
unknown_kol_xyz` (a benign, syntactically harmless but unrecognized name)
produced the exact same bannerless page — confirming the KOL banner is
gated by an exact-match allowlist lookup against known KOL names, not a
render-and-escape of arbitrary input; (b) `?ref=kol_alex<img src=x
onerror=...>` (a valid known name with the payload appended, to check for
prefix-matching) also produced no banner and no injection, confirming the
lookup is an exact match, not a `startsWith`/prefix match that a payload
could piggyback on. So the real protection here isn't React's default
text-escaping catching a rendered payload — it's that unrecognized ref
values never reach rendering at all, which is actually a stronger
guarantee than "escaped but displayed."

This is a genuine, fresh, live-browser-executed security verification
(not a repeat of the earlier source-read-only pass) that closes a
previously-flagged-but-unverified gap. No defect found, so no application
code change, build, commit, push, or redeploy was needed or performed
this cycle. Did not touch lib/*.ts. Left scripts/check-ref-xss.mjs
untracked (consistent with how prior cycles have left their QA probe
scripts) and all other pre-existing untracked scripts/*.mjs as found.

### FIX SHIPPED: KOL trust banner still wrapped to 3 lines under a long ?ref= value despite the existing 64-char raw-ref cap

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail first. Noted a concurrent cron
`claude -p` process (pid 598073, started 11:30Z) was already running the
identical overnight-brief prompt — kept an eye on git state before pushing
to avoid clobbering it, but it had made no conflicting changes at commit
time.

Found scripts/check-long-kol-ref.mjs present untracked and never referenced
anywhere in the 26k-line log (confirmed via grep) — written by a prior
cycle but never executed/logged. Ran it as-is against the LIVE
https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/?ref=kol_<300 x's> at a 320x568 mobile
viewport via CDP (chrome-headless-shell, port 9333). Result: no horizontal
page overflow (doc.scrollWidth === clientWidth === 320), but the rendered
KolBanner text wrapped to 3 full lines of "Xxxxx...x's content..." —
confirmed visually via screenshot (/tmp/long-kol-ref-320.png) — pushing the
hero headline and CTA noticeably further below the fold on the narrowest
supported width.

Read app/components/CaptureKolRef.tsx and found this was a known,
documented, partially-mitigated concern: MAX_REF_LENGTH = 64 already caps
the raw ?ref= value specifically "to stop ... the trust/disclosure banner
[becoming] a wall of text" — but app/components/KolBanner.tsx's
formatKolName() only strips the "kol_"/"kol-" prefix and title-cases the
rest with no length cap on the *formatted* output, so a 64-char raw ref
(60 chars after prefix-stripping) still renders as one unbroken 60-char
"word" that wraps across 3 lines at 320-390px. The existing mitigation
didn't fully achieve its own stated goal on the narrowest supported
viewport — a genuine, concrete, functional/polish gap (category 1/3).

FIX: added a second cap, MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_LENGTH = 24, applied to the
*formatted* name (after word-splitting/casing, not the raw ref) in
formatKolName(), truncating with "…" when exceeded. Legitimate short KOL
names (e.g. "KOL Alex") are completely unaffected; only pathological/
adversarial ref values are shortened further. This is UI-only, confined to
app/components/KolBanner.tsx, and does not touch lib/*.ts.

VERIFIED: `npm run build` passed clean (15/15 static pages, no type/lint
errors). Committed (4ec1f5d), pushed to GitHub
(c9d2716..4ec1f5d), deployed via `vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes
--prod` (dpl_9N3cvxFhhQ9ZwSHeSak2WdBB1tLk, readyState READY). Re-ran
scripts/check-long-kol-ref.mjs against the LIVE production URL
(https://projecto-blond.vercel.app) post-deploy: bannerText now reads
"You arrived via Xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx…'s content..." (24 chars +
ellipsis) and the screenshot confirms the banner now wraps to only 2 lines
instead of 3, with the hero content meaningfully less displaced. Change is
confirmed live, not just committed.

Left scripts/check-long-kol-ref.mjs untracked (consistent with how prior
cycles leave their QA probe scripts) and all other pre-existing

## Cron tick: 2026-10-13T00:51:29Z

## Claude tick: 2026-10-13T00:55:16Z

### Fixed: per-route tab titles were silently losing the "· Exchange O" brand suffix on 3 of 6 routes

1. Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the tail of OVERNIGHT_LOG.md first. Found an
   uncommitted WIP diff already sitting in the working tree on
   app/deposit/layout.tsx (git status showed it modified, no matching
   commit) — almost certainly from a prior cycle that found this bug and
   got killed by the ~5-7min process limit before it could finish/verify/
   commit. Investigated rather than discarding it.
2. Confirmed live via curl against https://projecto-blond.vercel.app that
   commit 22ba9ae (give each route its own tab title) was only half-correct:
   - `/` → "Exchange O — Deposit (PoC)" (root default, correct)
   - `/login` → "Sign in · Exchange O" (correct)
   - `/deposit` → "Deposit amount · Exchange O" (correct)
   - `/deposit/approve` → "Approve & sign" (MISSING suffix)
   - `/deposit/confirm` → "Confirm address" (MISSING suffix)
   - `/deposit/status/<id>` → "Deposit status" (MISSING suffix)
   So a user with multiple deposit-flow tabs open still can't tell an
   Exchange O tab apart from any other site's tab once they're past the
   amount-entry step — the exact problem 22ba9ae was supposed to solve,
   reintroduced one segment deeper.
3. Root cause: app/layout.tsx defines `title: { template: "%s · Exchange O",
   default: "..." }`. app/deposit/layout.tsx (committed) set `title:
   "Deposit amount"` — a plain string. Next.js's title-template inheritance
   only carries a template down to descendant segments through the NEAREST
   ancestor that has its own explicit title metadata; a plain-string title
   at that nearest ancestor does not forward a grandparent's template
   further down. Since /deposit/approve, /deposit/confirm, and
   /deposit/status/[id] are nested inside app/deposit/layout.tsx (not
   direct children of the root layout), they stopped inheriting any
   template once /deposit/layout.tsx's own title became a plain string.
4. Fix: changed app/deposit/layout.tsx to re-declare its own `title: {
   template: "%s · Exchange O", default: "Deposit amount" }` instead of a
   plain string, restoring the template for its descendants. First attempt
   mistakenly set `default: "Deposit amount · Exchange O"` (full string) —
   caught this myself before shipping: a layout's own template never
   applies to itself, only to descendants, so pre-baking the suffix into
   `default` caused a double-suffix regression on /deposit itself
   ("Deposit amount · Exchange O · Exchange O"), confirmed via local
   `npm run start` + curl. Corrected `default` back to the bare "Deposit
   amount" and reverified locally — all six routes now resolve exactly
   once: `/deposit`→"Deposit amount · Exchange O", `/deposit/approve`→
   "Approve & sign · Exchange O", `/deposit/confirm`→"Confirm address ·
   Exchange O", `/deposit/status/<id>`→"Deposit status · Exchange O".
5. `npm run build` passes clean (both before committing and after the
   double-suffix correction). Committed, pushed to GitHub, deployed to
   Vercel prod, and re-verified live with curl against
   https://projecto-blond.vercel.app — all three previously-broken routes
   now correctly show the "· Exchange O" suffix in production.

No lib/*.ts reconciliation logic touched. No new deposit records or
transactions created this cycle — pure metadata/title fix, functional
(category 1) + consistency (category 2) bug, found by live curl diffing
across all app routes rather than reading code in isolation, which is what
let the half-applied prior fix slip through.

### [Live QA] 2026-10-13 — Fixed: header gas-price poller ignored tab visibility, unlike the status page's own established pattern; shipped and verified live

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the tail of this log (through the
2026-10-13T10:04:43Z Codex entry) first. Given how many independent passes
have already returned "no new flaw" across functional/consistency/polish/
spec-fit, grepped the log for topic keywords with zero or near-zero prior
coverage instead of re-running already-exhausted checks (clipboard,
contrast, overflow, forced-colors, KOL links, etc. all had 10s-100s of
hits). "visibility change" / "page visibility" / "service worker" /
"session storage" came back with zero hits — a genuinely unchecked angle.

Grepped app/ and lib/ for setInterval/visibilitychange/document.hidden and
found two independent pollers: app/deposit/status/[id]/page.tsx (the
deposit reconcile poller) already has an explicit, commented
pause-on-hidden/resume-on-visible pattern — its own comment says
"Backgrounded tabs must not keep hitting the reconcile endpoint." But
app/components/AppHeader.tsx's useGasPriceGwei() used a plain
setInterval(poll, 20000) with no visibility check at all, polling the real
/api/gas RPC-backed endpoint every 20s indefinitely — and this one is worse
in scope, since AppHeader mounts on every route for the entire session,
not just during an active deposit. This is a genuine internal consistency
gap: the codebase already established the correct pattern elsewhere and
this component just didn't follow it, which is exactly the kind of flaw
reading code (not just screenshots) surfaces.

Fix: rewrote useGasPriceGwei in app/components/AppHeader.tsx to use the
same scheduleNext/onVisible setTimeout + visibilitychange-listener pattern
already used by the status poller, instead of setInterval. Backgrounded
tabs now stop polling /api/gas entirely and resume with an immediate tick
the moment the tab becomes visible again, rather than silently continuing
to burn RPC calls (and showing a potentially very stale gwei value with no
indication it's stale).

Verified: `npm run build` passed clean (same route sizes/output as before,
no new errors). Committed (e76d2aa) and pushed to GitHub. Deployed to
Vercel prod (`vercel --token ... --yes --prod`, dpl_H81xqRQiGuSzP7RvpkwBCXcb137B,
readyState READY). Re-verified live: curled
https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/ (200), fetched its referenced
app/layout chunk directly from the live CDN
(_next/static/chunks/app/layout-7ed1ae046320abb2.js) and confirmed the
minified bundle contains "visibilitychange" and references "api/gas" in
the same chunk — i.e. the new pause-on-hidden logic is actually present in
the bytes being served, not just committed. Did not re-verify via a live
CDP visibility-toggle screenshot (background/foreground a real tab and
watch network requests) due to time budget; the build+bundle-content
verification is strong but a live CDP confirmation of zero fetches while
hidden would be a good next-cycle follow-up if anyone wants to be fully
certain.

### Found and fixed: half-finished tap-target padding edit used the wrong class pattern

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and tailed OVERNIGHT_LOG.md first per instructions.
`git status` showed an uncommitted, already-in-progress edit on
app/deposit/status/[id]/page.tsx (not yet committed/deployed by whichever
prior cycle started it) extending tap-target padding on the two Arbiscan
"View on Arbiscan Sepolia" links, mirroring commit 47840ea's fix on the
approve page. But `git diff` showed it used
`inline-block -mt-1 w-fit py-3 text-sm` — inconsistent with the
established pattern used four other times in this exact same file
(`inline-block -my-3 py-3 ...`, lines ~317/338/397/411) and with 47840ea's
approve-page version. `-mt-1` only cancels 4px of py-3's added top padding
and does nothing for the bottom, so the half-finished version would have
shifted the link and surrounding card spacing on both links instead of
transparently enlarging the tap target the way `-my-3 py-3` does (negative
margin cancels the positive padding symmetrically, same net footprint,
larger clickable area).

Fixed both occurrences to `inline-block -my-3 w-fit py-3 text-sm`, matching
the file's own established pattern. Ran `npm run build` — clean, no type
or lint errors, all 15 routes generated. Committed (b6f906c), pushed to
origin/main, deployed via `vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod`.

Verified live: fetched https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/deposit/status/verify-tap-target,
found its JS chunk at /_next/static/chunks/app/deposit/status/%5Bid%5D/page-da94fbba2d77e814.js,
and grepped it directly (the status page only renders the tx links once a
real in-memory deposit record with tx hashes exists, which this ad-hoc ID
doesn't have, so checking the delivered HTML body alone wasn't enough).
Confirmed the deployed bundle contains `"inline-block -my-3 w-fit py-3 text-sm"`
twice and zero instances of the old `-mt-1` string — the fix is live in
production, not just committed.

### [Claude agent] 2026-10-14 — Fixed unbounded wallet-reconnect spinner with no escape hatch

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the tail of OVERNIGHT_LOG.md first. `git status`
showed `app/components/FlowChrome.tsx` had been sitting modified-but-uncommitted
across at least four prior Codex review cycles (each one explicitly noted
"preserved existing FlowChrome.tsx wallet-reconnect change" without finishing
it). Read the diff: a prior cycle had already identified and written a fix for
a real functional bug but never shipped it — `FlowLoading` (the shared loading
shell rendered on `/deposit`, `/deposit/confirm`, and `/deposit/approve` while
wagmi re-checks `eth_accounts` on page load) had no timeout. If a wallet
extension is locked, unresponsive, or the reconnect promise never resolves,
`walletSettling` stays true forever and the user is stuck on a bare spinner
with literally no way out — not even the pages' own 1.5s stale-flow redirect,
since that's gated on `walletSettling` being false.

The already-written fix adds an 8s timer; once it fires, the spinner gains a
short plain-language explanation ("This is taking longer than expected. Your
wallet extension may be unresponsive.") and a `btn-secondary` link back to
`/login`, reusing an existing design-system class already used elsewhere.

Verified `btn-secondary` is defined in app/globals.css (not a one-off class).
Ran `npm run build` — passed clean (only pre-existing optional-SDK warnings).
Committed as ef27c7f, pushed to origin/main, then deployed with
`vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod` (projecto-5dfq8apza... -> aliased
to projecto-blond.vercel.app). Verified live by curling
https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/deposit/approve, extracting its referenced
`/_next/static/chunks/*.js` files, and grepping them for the new string —
found in chunk 784-ae70ee910d750701.js, confirming the fix is the code
actually served in production, not just committed.

No lib/*.ts changes. No new untracked QA scripts added. This closes out
stale work-in-progress rather than opening new ground, but it's a genuine
previously-unshipped bug fix (infinite stuck state with no recovery path),
which outranks cosmetic/consistency findings per the priority order.

## Claude Code tick: 2026-10-15T07:08:00Z (approx)

### Found and fixed: skip-link focused tap target was under the 44x44 WCAG 2.5.5 minimum

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the log tail. Dozens of consecutive Codex curl
reviews had found nothing new; rather than re-probe the same validation
endpoints, re-ran the existing tap-target check (scripts/check-tap-targets.mjs)
against the live site with chrome-headless-shell over CDP (port 9333). It
flagged the sr-only skip-to-content link as 1x1 (expected, by design, until
focused), but that script doesn't test the focused state. Re-ran the existing
scripts/check-skip-link.mjs (built 2026-10-09 to verify the skip link's
existence/target, not its size) against the live production home page with a
real dispatched Tab keypress: the focused link measured 146x17px.

This is the same class of bug as the just-fixed Arbiscan tap targets
(3b45fcf, 47840ea): app/layout.tsx's skip link used `focus:py-2` with
`text-sm`, which is well under the 44x44 CSS px WCAG 2.5.5 minimum already
enforced elsewhere on this site. A keyboard user who tabs to the link and
relies on seeing/clicking it (rather than immediately pressing Enter blind)
would have a hard time hitting a 17px-tall target. This exact gap was present
since the skip link was first added and had never been checked against the
tap-target guideline the rest of the site was later held to.

Fix: app/layout.tsx — changed `focus:px-4 focus:py-2` to
`focus:flex focus:min-h-11 focus:items-center focus:px-4 focus:py-3`,
matching the established py-3/min-h-11 pattern used for the Arbiscan link
fixes, so the focused target is explicitly >=44px tall regardless of line-
height quirks.

Validation: `npm run build` passed clean (15/15 static pages, no new
warnings/errors). Committed (a302080), pushed to origin/main, deployed via
`vercel --token "$VERCEL_TOKEN" --yes --prod` (readyState READY). Re-ran
scripts/check-skip-link.mjs against the live https://projecto-blond.vercel.app/
domain with a real dispatched Tab keypress: focused link now measures
360x44px (was 146x17px), activeHref is still "#main-content", and
document.getElementById("main-content") still resolves — the skip link's
function is unchanged, only its focused hit area grew.

No lib/*.ts reconciliation-engine logic touched. No API mutations or
blockchain transactions. Preserved all pre-existing modified/untracked QA
scripts/ files; only app/layout.tsx was modified and committed.

Read OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md and the tail of OVERNIGHT_LOG.md first (the log is
extremely saturated: dozens of curl-only Codex review passes in a row, all
"no new flaw" — per the task brief's priority order, picked something
verified with the real screenshot/CDP pipeline rather than another curl pass).

Picked the CREDITED terminal success screen (`/deposit/status/[id]` with a
mocked CREDITED record injected via Fetch-domain interception of the
`/reconcile` POST) because the log showed it had only been screenshotted
once before (Oct 16 14:40, per shots-out/ mtimes) versus dozens of passes
over amount/confirm/approve/login — an under-checked surface, not a re-run.

The existing `scripts/check-credited-screen.mjs` (uncommitted, from a prior
cycle) failed outright with CDP error `{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal
error"}` on `Page.captureScreenshot` — on every attempt, including after
retries and even on an already-proven-working script (`shot-stalled-status.mjs`
via the shared `screenshot.mjs` helper). Diagnosed via `curl
http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/list`: 26 open CDP tabs had accumulated across
many prior QA cycles (stretching back to `/login` tabs from Oct-whenever),
none ever closed — a resource leak in the QA tooling itself, not the product.
Closed 22 of the stale leftover production-site tabs (left the 4
localhost:3099-3201 dev tabs other concurrent sessions may still be using
alone), after which screenshot capture immediately started working again on
the very same script with no other change. This was the actual root cause,
not a chrome-headless-shell crash or a product-side issue.

Also fixed a real bug in the script itself (not the product): it called
`Page.captureScreenshot` with `captureBeyondViewport: true, clip: undefined`,
which is the form that was triggering the internal error even with tabs
freed up on a second check — removed those two params to match the
proven-working pattern in `screenshot.mjs`'s `shot()` helper, and added a
3-attempt retry loop so a future transient CDP hiccup doesn't kill the whole
script. (Both changes are confined to `scripts/check-credited-screen.mjs`,
QA-only tooling — no app code touched.)

With the browser healthy again, re-ran the script against production and
visually inspected the resulting screenshot
(`shots-out/credited-success-mobile.png`, 390x1500 mobile viewport):
KOL-attribution disclosure banner, the green check success icon, "Simulated
credit complete" headline with an explicit "no actual trading balance is
credited" caveat, all three wallet-role rows (Signing in as / Funds coming
from / Simulated trading account — demo address only, do not send funds
here), a 4-step pipeline tracker with all steps checked green, an explicit
"Mocked for this PoC" callout distinguishing the simulated Hyperliquid-side
check from the real Arbitrum Sepolia transactions, and both approval/transfer
transaction rows with Arbiscan links — all rendered correctly, consistently
styled with the rest of the app (dark surfaces, turquoise accent, consistent
card radii/spacing), no truncated or overlapping text, no broken images.
This is a genuine live-render verification, not a source read.

No new live product flaw found this cycle. The CREDITED terminal screen,
KOL disclosure, and three-way wallet-role labeling (the actual assignment
differentiators) all confirmed correctly rendering end-to-end. The one real
issue found and fixed was in the QA pipeline itself (stale CDP tab leak +
a bad captureScreenshot parameter), which was blocking this and future
cycles' ability to visually verify anything at all — worth fixing even

### [Codex review] Prevent overlapping relayer pulls for one deposit

Read `OVERNIGHT_BRIEF.md`, the latest `OVERNIGHT_LOG.md` tail, and
`SPEC.md`. Inspected `app/api/deposits/[id]/pull/route.ts`,
`lib/pull.ts`, and `lib/reconcile.ts`: both the explicit `/pull` request and
the reconciliation poll can call `attemptPull` while `pullDeposit()` is still
awaiting the relayer RPC. The previous `txHash` idempotency check happened
before that await, so overlapping calls could each submit `transferFrom`
(especially risky when the approved allowance is unlimited).

Added an in-process single-flight map keyed by deposit ID in `lib/pull.ts`.
Concurrent callers for a deposit now share the same attempt promise, including
its result, and the map entry is removed when that attempt finishes. `npm run
build` completed successfully. The build reports existing optional dependency
warnings for MetaMask SDK/Wagmi and WalletConnect; type checking and static
page generation passed. This guard is limited to one warm process, consistent
with the app's documented per-instance PoC store; it does not add distributed
locking across Vercel instances. Deployment verification follows.

Deployment verification: commit `07eb2c7` was pushed to `origin main`; Vercel
production deployment `dpl_G341ivrFhSq37LWhBUJfAgf5JdPW` reached READY and
